overview: North Macedonia is the modern state that became independent from Yugoslavia in 1991. Its imported map begins in 1994 and should not be confused with the ancient Macedonian kingdom or the wider geographical region. Its communities combine inherited crafts and performances with modern schools, museums and institutions.

periods.title: An independent republic
periods.summary: The former Yugoslav republic became a separate state and entered the United Nations in 1993.

periods.title: North Macedonia
periods.summary: The name agreement with Greece took effect in 2019; NATO membership followed in 2020.

items.text: Kopachkata is a social dance from Dramche in the Pijanec region. Dancers form a semicircle and hold one another’s belts, with crossed arms. The shared formation requires people to coordinate their movement, rather than each dancer choosing an independent route across the floor.

The dance moves from walking into small quick steps and more energetic movements. In its digging figure, the left foot repeatedly strikes the ground while the dancer balances on the right. The name and footwork make sense together when the dancers disturb the dust.

Experienced dancers guide beginners, who can watch the steps and gradually take more demanding positions. Weddings and public or religious celebrations provide occasions to perform. The practice passes on movement, music and a way of taking part in community gatherings.

Skopje’s Museum of Contemporary Art grew from international solidarity after the 1963 earthquake, before the present republic became independent. An artists’ association called for donated works to help the city rebuild its cultural life. The collection preserves that response across later political changes.

The museum opened its new building in 1970, providing a permanent home for the collection. Earlier exhibitions had occupied rented space downtown. Building a museum required rooms, conservation and organisation alongside the generosity of artists who sent their work.

Its early programme included the graphic work of Picasso and exhibitions of Pop Art alongside Macedonian and other Yugoslav artists. Local artists encountered different ways of making images through these displays. The institution became a meeting point for national and international art.

sections.title: The details that help a child learn

items.text: In a 2024 UNICEF interview, Hristina described how visual displays and assistive technology helped her autistic daughter learn in a mainstream school. The example shows how the arrangement and equipment of a classroom can matter as much as the lessons written on a timetable.

Educational assistants receive guidance from resource centres, including teaching materials, exercises and advice from mentors. These centres developed from former special schools after changes in education policy. Their role is to help children participate in regular school communities.

Hristina also described cooperation between teachers and parents, and regular review of her daughter’s support. She stressed that suitable education should be a right rather than a matter of luck. This is one family’s account of progress and continuing needs.

An official banknote specification records the Macedonian words “десет денари”, meaning “ten denars”. They are printed in Cyrillic on the ten-denar note. This small sample comes from a documented modern object used for payment, rather than an invented greeting.

The same banknote design uses an ancient marble torso as its main image and tiny repeated letters among its security details. Modern printing turns a cultural object into an image many people can handle. The ancient sculpture and the modern currency belong to different historical periods.

sections.title: A name changes, a state continues

items.text: The agreement with Greece resolved the country’s international name dispute, with the relevant procedures completed in February 2019. North Macedonia joined NATO in March 2020. These were diplomatic changes in a continuing state, not the creation of a new population.

ending.text: The republic continues under the name North Macedonia. The 2019 name change altered its official designation, while its communities, institutions and independent statehood continued.
